precepts.text: Amos was no prophet, neither a prophet's son, but an herdman and a gatherer of sycomore fruit, and the Lord took him as he followed the flock and said, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.
precepts.point: The same pattern continues through the prophets: Elisha was taken from the plow and Amos from the herd.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
Amos was taken from the herd: “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit: And the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.”

The Lord took him as he followed the flock, as he took David from the sheep, and sent him to prophesy unto his people Israel.

precepts.text: Amaziah the priest of Bethel tries to drive the prophet Amos out of the king's chapel, telling him to prophesy in Judah instead, which shows how the northern kingdom rejected the true word.
precepts.point: This is the setting for a division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After the split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry and forsook the Levites, so a prophet of the Most High would want nothing to do with their manner of worship.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
“Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.” Amos had said, “Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.”

So Amaziah told the prophet, “O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.” The priest of Bethel drove the prophet out of the king’s chapel.

That shows how the northern kingdom rejected the true word. The king’s chapel had its own priests and its own prophets, and the word of the Most High was not welcome there; which is why Ahab could gather four hundred prophets who all said the same thing.

points: Notice what's being said here by Amos, but notice the actions of Amaziah. Amaziah was more concerned with protecting the king's institution instead of hearing the word of the Lord. And it's the same thing that's going on today. Why? Because the things written afore time was written for our learning. Instead of correcting the leaders or some of the teachers in these congregations with their ridiculous doctrines or ridiculous accusations, they prefer we not speak at all. It's the same thing here that we reading with Amaziah and Amos.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: A plumb line is used for measuring. Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more; I'mma cut them off. The high places of Isaac shall be desolate: that's the southern kingdom. And the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste: northern kingdom. And I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
